page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 118 GB NVMe SSD, and the virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is rated as average, whereas multi-core performance falls into the bottom 10%, reflecting the physical limitation of its single-core, dual-thread allocation. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show weak read-only performance at 168.1 GB/sec for small blocks and 22.92 GB/sec for large blocks, alongside a poor write speed of 12.15 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and database operations scores are weak, though the Passmark memory score remains in the average tier.

This instance is configured for workloads requiring higher memory density relative to compute power, such as small-scale database operations, caching layers, or lightweight web serving. However, the low multi-core compute capacity and weak memory write bandwidth present clear bottlenecks for parallel processing or write-heavy applications. It supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which assist in specific vector and matrix operations, as shown by its average performance in small-model LLM text generation.
description: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. This x86_64 instance utilizes Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. While its single-core CPU performance and Passmark memory scores sit in the average tier, its multi-core performance and memory write bandwidth are limited, falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarks. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core makes it suitable for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads such as small databases, caching systems, and lightweight web serving. However, parallel processing tasks are constrained by the single physical core architecture.
